answer: If I could meet any famous person, it would probably be a well-known entrepreneur whose story I find genuinely inspiring. He is famous for building a huge technology company from almost nothing, starting out with a handful of friends and very little money. What fascinates me, though, is not the wealth but the [[perseverance]] behind it. I have read a great deal about him, in interviews and in a biography I borrowed from a friend, and I know how many times he failed before succeeding, which I find strangely reassuring. Several of his early ventures went bankrupt, and at one point even people close to him thought he should give up. What draws me to him is his reputation for thinking in genuinely [[unconventional]] ways, seeing opportunities others dismiss. As for why I would like to meet him, I would love to ask how he stayed motivated during the years when everything seemed to be collapsing. I imagine he would be surprisingly [[down-to-earth]], because people who have struggled tend to be. Since I studied business administration, I would also be curious to hear what he thinks young people in a country like Bangladesh should focus on. I think a single conversation with someone like that could be more [[enlightening]] than any book. Realistically it will never happen, but if it did, I would come prepared with a long list of questions and simply listen. Even a few minutes with him would give me a story to tell my family for years.

followUps.q: Would you like to be famous yourself?
followUps.answer: Not really. I think fame brings a lot of pressure and very little privacy. I would much rather be respected by the people around me than recognised by strangers in the street.

followUps.q: Do you think famous people are good role models?
followUps.answer: Some are, especially those who worked hard and stayed humble. But many are admired for the wrong reasons, so young people need to be quite [[discerning]] about whose example they follow.
